Source. The staged witness starts with `ff d8 ff ca`, so `get_sof(..., TRUE, TRUE)` both stores progressive-arithmetic dispatch state and materializes `data_precision = 8`, `image_height = 0x0120`, `image_width = 0x0d20`, and `num_components = 4` from the SOF10 body. Those frame fields size the later transform workspace, while the mode flags steer `jpeg_read_coefficients()` into the arithmetic decoder path used by the bug.

The only SOS body is `01 20 20 10 2c 06`, so `get_sos()` records a one-component scan with selector `0x20`, tables DC=2/AC=0, `Ss=16`, `Se=44`, `Ah=0`, and `Al=6`. Those scan parameters are the state later consumed by `start_pass()` and by the coefficient-scaling store in `decode_mcu_AC_first()`.

Before coefficient decoding begins, the saved stack's frame 5 shows the crashing path is the third `tjTransform()` call at `fuzz/transform.cc:129`, whose caller has already set `TJXOP_ROT90 | TJXOPT_TRIM` at lines 121-122. For that transform, `jtransform_request_workspace()` allocates transposed `workspace_coef_arrays`, so the later output path has separate rotated destination buffers available instead of re-encoding `srccoefs` in place.

Parser-admitted checkpoint. Because step 1 made the image progressive arithmetic and step 2 set `Ah=0` with `Ss=16`, `start_pass()` selects `decode_mcu_AC_first()` rather than the DC-first or refinement arms.

While `jpeg_read_coefficients()` is absorbing the scan, `consume_data()` maps the current `coef->whole_image` rows and stores direct block pointers into `coef->MCU_buffer`. The arithmetic decoder will therefore write coefficient values straight into the persistent source virtual arrays rather than into a scratch copy.

Tainted-value origin. On the witnessed path, `decode_mcu_AC_first()` materializes a malformed nonzero AC coefficient and stores it through step 5's alias into `coef->whole_image`. The arithmetic decoder simply shifts the decoded signed magnitude by `Al=6` and truncates it to `JCOEF`; it does not enforce the later baseline-Huffman `MAX_COEF_BITS` bound.

Output-side reinitialization checkpoint. On the same third transform call, `jpeg_copy_critical_parameters()` copies the source frame shape, component count, and precision into `dstinfo`, and `jpeg_set_defaults(dstinfo)` is the point where the output side switches away from arithmetic coding and back to default baseline Huffman tables before any coefficient writeout.

After step 7 has reinitialized the destination compressor, `jtransform_adjust_parameters()` returns step 3's workspace arrays as `dstcoefs` instead of returning `srccoefs`. Earlier in the same function, the `JXFORM_ROT_90` arm also transposes the destination parameters, so these arrays represent the rotated output image.

When `jpeg_write_coefficients(cinfo, dstcoefs)` runs on the third transform call, the compression-side coefficient controller saves step 8's returned workspace arrays as `coef->whole_image`. That is the destination coefficient buffer that `compress_output()` later walks.

This is the actual source-to-destination coefficient transfer. `do_rot_90()` fills step 8's workspace arrays by transposing source coefficients and negating every other source row in the mirrorable area. The out-of-range coefficient from step 6 is therefore materialized in a rotated destination block with the same absolute magnitude even if the sign flips.

On the baseline-Huffman output path created by step 7, `start_pass_huff()` derives the active AC table. `jpeg_make_c_derived_tbl()` allocates a `c_derived_tbl` when needed, zeros `ehufco[256]` and `ehufsi[256]`, and populates only symbols 0..255, so symbol 256 is out of range by construction.

During `jpeg_finish_compress()`, `compress_output()` maps the encoder-side `coef->whole_image` from step 9 and hands block pointers from the rotated destination arrays to `encode_mcu_huff()` / `encode_one_block()`. This is the output-side alias that reconnects the transformed destination block to the sink.

Root cause. When the rotated destination block from step 12 reaches the C Huffman encoder, the transformed out-of-range coefficient from step 10 becomes `temp`. Because step 10 preserved absolute magnitude, `JPEG_NBITS_NONZERO(temp)` can still return 16 here, and vulnerable code does not reject `nbits > MAX_COEF_BITS`.

Repeated executions of this zero branch on the same transformed destination block increment `r` once per zero immediately before the bad coefficient. The saved stack narrows the crashing coefficient only to the line-594 macro group, but whichever one of those six `kloop(...)` arms fires, the destination zigzag walk has accumulated a 15-zero run at that point.

This combines the zero run and coefficient width into the AC symbol index. Because step 14 has already left `r = 15` and step 13 allowed `nbits = 16`, the overflowing value here is `temp3 = 256`, one past the legal AC symbol range 0..255.

Sink. `actbl->ehufsi` has 256 entries, so step 15's `temp3 = 256` reads one byte past the table into adjacent image-pool storage and produces the observed `use-of-uninitialized-value`. MemorySanitizer reports the corresponding macro call site at `jchuff.c:594:3` because this line executes inside the unrolled `kloop(...)` expansion group on that source line.

Root cause. The vulnerable C Huffman encoder computes the bit width of a nonzero AC coefficient from the rotated destination block but never checks that the width stays within `MAX_COEF_BITS` before combining it with the zero run into a Huffman symbol index. For the witnessed transformed coefficient, this missing guard lets `nbits` reach 16 and eventually yields symbol 256.

MSAN sink. Once the derived AC symbol for the rotated destination block becomes 256, this read indexes one byte past the 256-entry `ehufsi` table and consumes adjacent image-pool bytes that were never initialized as table data.
